case_title: Chaman Lal v. The State of Himachal Pradesh
aggravating_circumstances: Mental illness of the victim, taking advantage of her condition
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted on grounds of delay in FIR and victim's mental state
high_court_outcome: Reversed acquittal and convicted for offences under Sections 376 and 506 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, a man, was alleged to have committed sexual assault on a woman who was mentally retarded. The victim, who was 19 years old, was found to have an IQ of 62, indicating mild mental retardation. The victim became pregnant as a result of the assault, and the accused was identified as the biological father of the child. The victim did not disclose the incident due to fear and mental weakness. The prosecution presented medical evidence, including testimony from psychiatrists, to establish the victim's mental state. The trial court acquitted the accused, citing delay in the FIR and the victim's mental state. The High Court reversed the acquittal, finding that the victim was not in a position to understand the consequences of the sexual assault and that the accused had taken advantage of her mental condition.
